text:
Short answer: on bandwidth alone, yes; on the FMECA, not yet. All figures below are DEMO placeholders from the synthetic test input, not real project values.

Bandwidth. Side A has 10 hoists with 2 SWS units each, and each unit sends 100 kbps of logger data (DEMO). The sws.fibre_load tool puts that at 2.0 Mbps on the 1000 Mbps side A fibre link, a fraction of 0.002 (DEMO). Logger traffic is therefore negligible against the link rate. Note that SWS has no fibre of its own: each unit reaches its base station over RS-485 duplex on CAT cable, so the proposal is that the base stations forward the data onto the fibre next to PROFINET. The existing PROFINET load, cycle times and device count on side A were not supplied, so cycle-time margin has not been checked.

FMECA. No FMECA document, ratings or segregation assumptions were found in the supplied material, so we cannot show the FMECA is unbroken. What we can do is close the two open red items in the register with a stated design change, and then the FMECA has to be reissued with that design:

- DEMO-NET-001 (broadcast storm from an SWS port): the switch ports that carry logger traffic get storm control (broadcast/multicast rate limit) and ingress rate limiting sized to the 100 kbps per unit (DEMO), with the port disabled on exceedance. The base station is the only device on that port (one MAC, port security). These ports are currently [OPEN] in the switch configuration; the mitigation is to specify them this way before anything is connected.
- DEMO-NET-002 (SWS traffic reaches the PLC VLAN): logger traffic goes in a dedicated VLAN separate from the PLC/PROFINET VLAN, with no routing between them and the logger uplink as the only member besides the base-station ports. The PROFINET VLAN keeps its priority (QoS) so logger frames can never delay cyclic traffic. If the fibre runs a media-redundancy ring (MRP/MRPD, not supplied), the logger VLAN must not be allowed to interfere with the ring protocol; this has to be confirmed against the actual topology.

What is still needed before this is accepted: the latest approved FMECA and its entries on the side A fibre, switches and loss of communication; the existing PROFINET load, cycle times and device list; the fibre topology and redundancy scheme; any contractual or class-society segregation requirement on SWS communication; and the decision on PoE for SWS, which is [OPEN] pending Ex requirements. Until those are in hand the answer is: technically feasible at 0.002 of the link (DEMO), conditional on the two mitigations above and a reissued FMECA.

text: The conditional conclusion is reasonable, but the QoS guarantee is false and the proposed mitigations do not yet demonstrate FMECA compliance.

findings.text: The claim that QoS means logger frames can never delay cyclic PROFINET traffic is incorrect. On ordinary non-preemptive Ethernet, a logger frame already transmitting can delay a higher-priority frame. Acceptability requires checking actual switch scheduling, link speeds, traffic bounds and PROFINET timing requirements.

VLAN separation and port policing do not establish that sharing preserves the FMECA. Shared fibre, switches, power and control-plane resources introduce or retain common failure paths. The approved FMECA must assess these dependencies before the two register items can be considered closed.

Sizing a base-station port limit to 100 kbps per unit requires the number of units aggregated by that station, protocol overhead and burst characteristics. The proposed disable-on-exceedance behavior also needs failure-effect assessment because legitimate bursts could disconnect the station.

The cited source contents and tool result were not provided for review, so their support for the topology, register entries and calculated inputs cannot be verified. The stated arithmetic itself is consistent.
